original_question: Are Absent tibia-polydactyly-arachnoid cyst syndrome and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease caused by the same chromosomal abnormalities?

final_qi.question: What chromosomal abnormalities are associated with Absent tibia-polydactyly-arachnoid cyst syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: All reported individuals with the triad of absent tibia, pre-axial polydactyly and arachnoid (TAC) cyst carry structural abnormalities that remove or disrupt the distal long-arm of chromosome 6 (classically 6q23-q26), including interstitial/terminal 6q deletions or a t(6;13)(q23;q22) translocation. Loss of genes in this distal 6q segment is therefore regarded as the causal chromosomal defect in Absent tibia-polydactyly-arachnoid cyst syndrome.

final_qi.question: What chromosomal abnormalities are associated with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease?
final_qi.long_answer: The commonest form of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT1A) is caused by a 1.4-megabase tandem duplication encompassing the PMP22 gene on chromosome 17p11.2-p12. This chromosomal duplication increases PMP22 dosage, leading to the demyelinating peripheral neuropathy characteristic of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

This chromosomal duplication increases PMP22 dosage, leading to the demyelinating peripheral neuropathy characteristic of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

Absent tibia-polydactyly-arachnoid cyst syndrome is caused by deletions or disruptions in the distal long arm of chromosome 6 (6q23-q26), while Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease is typically caused by a duplication of the PMP22 gene region on chromosome 17 (17p11.2-p12). Since these alterations involve different chromosomes and distinct genetic defects, they are not caused by the same chromosomal abnormalities.
